name: New Hampshire Orchid Society Conservation and Education Grant
summary: Small one-time grants for specific projects that directly benefit orchid conservation. Individuals and organisations can apply; society members get priority but membership is not required.

steps: NHOS Board of Directors review and vote

eligibility.rule: Requesting a specific project, not general funding within a larger project
Not using the grant for conference speaker, attendee or travel expenses
Funds administered and accounted for by a not-for-profit organisation
Project has not already received an NHOS grant

documents: Two written recommendations from people not directly involved in the project

status.quote: Applications are accepted at any time.

applicant_types.quote: This is an opportunity for both individuals and organizations to be specific in requesting funds.

access.quote: Applications may be sent by email to conservation@nhorchids.org

window.quote: Applications are accepted at any time.

amount.quote: Range of grant monies is from $100-$1000.

effort.quote: Applications may be sent by email to conservation@nhorchids.org or by postal mail to:
Applications are presented to the Conservation and Education Committee for review
and then brought before the NHOS Board of Directors who vote on whether to request clarification, approve, modify or deny the Grant.

eligibility.quote: Request must be specific, "general funding" within a much larger project will not be awarded.
This grant process is specifically not to be used to cover speaker or attendee expenses at conferences or gatherings, nor any conference-related travel expenses.
NHOS policy as a not-for profit, requires administration and accounting of the funds by another not-for -profit.
Grants shall be one-time per project awards.

after_award.quote: This report may include a talk at a Society meeting or show, a written report, photo essay etc. and shall be scheduled and completed within 1 year of receiving the grant unless an extension is authorized by NHOS.

documents.quote: Two written recommendations are required by someone who is not directly involved with the project attesting to the relevance of the project and the qualifications of the applicant including their reliability to fulfill the terms of the grant.
